Not a blocker and not a defect. A side project — working name

— is being opened to derive the general principles this build has been producing as a by-product, and to state them as a protocol for building open-source tools that serve industrial ecosystems and the people working in them. The atlas is the evidence base for that work, which is why it is being set down at a clean boundary rather than mid-stage.

Pausing here is cheap in a way it would not have been three days ago. Plan 1 is merged and plan 2 is designed but unstarted, so nothing is half-built: the boundary between "decided" and "constructed" currently falls exactly at the working-tree edge. The cost of the pause is carried almost entirely by item 2 above, which is now a fortnight-old known falsehood sitting in an append-only record — the longer it stands uncorrected, the more it resembles the very failure mode the log convention exists to prevent.
